title: Upcoming IPOs, Explained Simply — July 2026
description: This month, we're looking at IPOs from Knack Packaging Limited and IC Electricals Company Limited. You'll learn what an IPO is, why companies do them, and how.

faq.q: How do I even apply for an IPO?
faq.a: You can apply for an IPO through your bank's ASBA (Applications Supported by Blocked Amount) facility via net banking, or through your stockbroker's platform. Your money remains blocked in your account until allotment, and is only debited if you receive shares.
The lot size is the minimum number of shares you must bid for in an IPO. You cannot apply for fewer shares than the lot size, and you must apply in multiples of it.

faq.q: What is the difference between Mainboard and SME IPOs?
faq.a: Mainboard IPOs are for larger, more established companies and are listed on the main exchanges (NSE, BSE). SME IPOs are for smaller companies and are listed on separate platforms like NSE Emerge or BSE SME, often with different listing and trading rules.

faq.q: Can I sell my shares on the listing day?
faq.a: Yes, once your allotted shares are credited to your demat account and the company lists on the stock exchange, you can sell them on the listing day itself, just like any other stock.

faq.q: What happens if I don't get an allotment?
faq.a: If you don't receive any shares in the allotment process, the money that was blocked in your bank account for the IPO application will be unblocked, usually within a few days after the allotment date.
